input.quote: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer of USD 25,000 per day for "any delay in providing a dependency" — uncapped in amount and duration, and triggered by even minor or immaterial delays. This fails the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) and also fails the fallback, which permits only a capped early-termination fee of three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount; an unbounded daily charge can readily exceed remaining contract value, which is walk-away territory. No offsetting service credits or Vendor-side liquidated damages appear elsewhere in the document, and the liability cap in Section 21.1 does not clearly shield Customer from this fee obligation. Redline deletes the Customer-payable LD and substitutes an equitable schedule/Fee adjustment via change order, with the three-month early-termination-fee cap offered as fallback.

proposal.summary: Remove Customer-payable liquidated damages for dependency delay; substitute equitable schedule adjustment
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, and an uncapped USD 25,000 per day charge for any dependency delay is far beyond our position. We have replaced it with an equitable adjustment of the affected dates; if a fixed amount is essential, we could consider an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount.

ops.oldText: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
ops.newText: Customer is not liable for liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement. If Customer's delay in providing an agreed dependency materially affects Vendor's performance, the affected dates and, where applicable, the affected Fees will be equitably adjusted through a change order, provided Vendor promptly notifies Customer of the delay and mitigates its effect.
